grunt: Improve safe state when entering DP mode When configuring DisplayPort alt mode, follow the spec more closely: Place the USB Type-C pins that are to be re-configured to DisplayPort Configuration into the Safe state before sending the configure command. Then switch the pins to DisplayPort after receiving the ack to the command. For TYPEC_MUX_DOCK, the superspeed signals can remain connected. For TYPEC_MUX_DP, disconnect the superspeed signals in svdm_dp_config, then re-configure the pins to DisplayPort in svdm_dp_post_config. This means we avoid an unnecessary disconnection in the TYPEC_MUX_DOCK case (CL:1553572) but still follow the spec and put the pins in safe state in the TYPEC_MUX_DP case. arc: validate decoded output video by golden frame-wise MD5 VideoFrame is implemented for converting output frame data into I420 pixel format cropping visible window. In order to compute MD5 and validate with golden one in frame-wise, and ouput to raw file if needed. For ARC++N, output buffer will return YUV_420_FLEXIBLE as color format which may be either NV12 or YV12 underneath. In this case, we need to try converting from both formats and match the golden MD5 to find out the right format. This requires to be done in the first output frame and then adopt to the whole stream. Golden frame-wise MD5 is read from the text file which should be named as <test-input-name>.frames.md5, and located in the same directory. network_WiFi_Reset: make 'reboot' and 'cleanup()' mutually exclusive WiFiCellTestBase's cleanup() isn't very resilient to reboots/crashes -- among other things, it uses an xmlrpc connection for the DUT, which doesn't like unexpected reboots; it also doesn't like the DUT WiFi device disappearing underneath it. All of this make it hard to support "reboot as a cleanup method" in conjunction with "parent's cleanup()". Since the cleanup() routine is somewhat optional (it's nice to re-set state and tear down the AP, but subsequent tests should also take care of re-initializing anything they care about), let's just make "reboot" and "cleanup" mutually exclusive. While we're at it, I noticed that on some (badly-supported) devices, we're fairly likely to crash the kernel at some point, so extend this to check for the boot ID -- if we've rebooted during unexpectedly the test, we can also skip the cleanup. This partially reverts/reworks commit aeca0c168f67685f8075812ec50047d845400a4d ("network_WiFi_Reset: perform WiFiCellTestBase cleanup before reboot"), since it didn't do its job very well.
